description: Manage leave requests: list, get, create, update, cancel, approve, reject, view types and allowances. Approve or reject only requests whose time-off approver is you: pending does not mean pending for you, and a credential that would let a decision through does not make another approver's request yours. You are the employee who logged in, or under a company API key the employee in FACTORIAL_EMPLOYEE_ID. list_leaves and get_leave show each leave's approver (timeoff_manager_id, timeoff_manager_name) and routed_to_me; list_leaves with pending_for_me: true returns exactly the requests awaiting your decision. approve and reject refuse a leave routed to someone else, or any leave when the server does not know who you are. A decision is recorded in Factorial under whoever made it, so approve and reject are refused under a company API key unless the operator has set FACTORIAL_ALLOW_COMPANY_KEY_APPROVALS=true. Attribution: a write is recorded in Factorial under the credential that made it. With a user login that is you. With only a company API key it is the key's account, not under you, and the confirmation step and the result of every such write say so; tell the user before relying on it.

confirmation_token.description: Token from an override_approver preview; repeat the same arguments with it to execute

finish_on.description: End date (YYYY-MM-DD). For list_leaves: leaves overlapping a window to this date

override_approver.description: For approve/reject: decide a leave that is not routed to you. Only when you have been asked to act on that approver's behalf, never because the leave is merely pending. Needs override_reason. The first call writes nothing and returns a preview and a confirmation_token

override_reason.description: Required with override_approver: who asked you to decide this request and why. Recorded in the audit log; not sent to Factorial or to the employee

pending_for_me.description: For list_leaves: only leaves still awaiting a decision whose time-off approver is you (the logged-in user, or FACTORIAL_EMPLOYEE_ID). Reads every page, so page and limit are ignored; start_on, finish_on and employee_id still narrow it

start_on.description: Start date (YYYY-MM-DD). For list_leaves: leaves overlapping a window from this date
